_comment: Shared by api/tests/test_summary.py and web/tests/summary.test.cjs: the text message (api/pipeline.py) and the replay/cards (web/lib/summary.ts) must say the same thing for the same run. 'today' is when the question was asked.

cases.name: big one-time purchase, short dip that recovers
cases.verdict: Heads up: spending $2,000 on Oct 17 would be a real stretch.
cases.dip: Most likely you'd drop below $0 the week of Oct 31, bottom out around $799 short, and stay there for about 2 weeks before your paychecks catch up.

cases.name: recurring cost, small risk increase
cases.verdict: Adding $60 a month starting today looks manageable.
cases.dip: If it does go wrong, the tight spot is most likely the week of Oct 24.

cases.name: no risk at all
cases.verdict: Spending $250 tomorrow looks safe. Your balance stayed above $0 in every simulation.

cases.name: already tight without the purchase
cases.verdict: Your cash is already tight, with or without this.

cases.name: middle risk, later date
cases.verdict: Spending $500 on Dec 1 is doable, but worth a second look.
cases.dip: If it does go wrong, the tight spot is most likely the week of Nov 7.

cases.name: next year, never recovers
cases.verdict: Heads up: spending $3,000 on Jan 18, 2027 would be a real stretch.
cases.dip: Most likely you'd drop below $0 the week of Nov 7, bottom out around $1,250 short, and stay there for about a week.
